title: The Handwriting
summary: June hangs up the phone that whispered your name and warns you never to answer. She reveals she missed her stop in 1987 because a figure wearing her mother's coat waited on the platform, and she has ridden the train ever since. You glance at the rules again and recognize the handwriting as your own — the loops, the crossed sevens. In the black window your reflection keeps reading after you look up, then blinks first; you look away just in time. The route map flickers and the next stop changes to your name. The train slows, June begs you not to get off, and through the opening doors your mother waves, smiling too wide.

continuity_out: Night 1, still 2:14 AM. You sit beside June with the rules (your handwriting) and a ticket with one hole. The route map now shows your name as the next stop. The train is slowing. June grips your wrist, begging you not to get off, repeating her mistake. The doors have opened onto a platform where your mother stands waving, smiling too wide — the same figure June described from 1987. The conductor is somewhere behind, moving toward the last car.
